item.question: The panel analyst argues that an exchange promise would help Northstar more than a longer refund window. How much more often do Gen Z shoppers return athletic apparel than shoppers over 35 according to the panel, and what exchange guarantee does the FY27 memo propose, and for when?

standard.answer_markdown:

According to the panel, Gen Z shoppers return athletic apparel at roughly 1.5 times the rate of shoppers over 35 [[NORTHSTAR/ANALYST-CALL@v1:S1.B1]]. The FY27 memo proposes a cross-category Fit Promise, a free exchange guarantee covering every apparel and footwear size, to launch in Q1 FY27 [[NORTHSTAR/FY27-MEMO@v1:S1.B6]].

### Key findings

- Panel data show Gen Z shoppers return athletic apparel at roughly 1.5 times the rate of shoppers over 35, concentrated in leggings, tops and multi-brand sizing, and much smaller in footwear [[NORTHSTAR/ANALYST-CALL@v1:S1.B1]].
- The analyst thought a clear exchange promise would help more than a longer refund window for a brand in Northstar's position, because most customer cost lies in time and uncertainty rather than money [[NORTHSTAR/ANALYST-CALL@v1:S1.B1]].
- The memo's Fit Promise is a free exchange guarantee covering every apparel and footwear size, planned for Q1 FY27 [[NORTHSTAR/FY27-MEMO@v1:S1.B6]].
- The guarantee would be backed by a unified grading standard so the promise is credible and exchange costs are contained [[NORTHSTAR/FY27-MEMO@v1:S1.B6]].
- The memo budgets $4.5 million for the Fit Promise launch and fit education content [[NORTHSTAR/FY27-MEMO@v1:S1.B7]].

### Interpretation

The memo's exchange-based design is consistent with the analyst's view that an exchange promise suits Northstar better than a longer refund window [inference]. Because Gen Z bracketing is common in apparel, an exchange guarantee could raise order volumes of multiple sizes, which the memo itself flags as a risk [inference].

### Gaps & unknowns

The panel figure is described by the analyst as an estimate, better for direction than exact levels, and the underlying cut by age band and category had not yet been supplied [inference]. The evidence does not show Northstar's own apparel return rates for comparison. It also does not show whether an exchange guarantee changes ordering behaviour [inference]. The brand strategy document lists this as untested, so a controlled test or Northstar return data would close that gap.

item.question: How much do young shoppers care about fast delivery, and is Northstar's personalization offer creating delivery friction? Give the trend panel's share of Gen Z rating three-day delivery essential and how much more likely personalized orders were to trigger order-status tickets.

standard.answer_markdown:
### Answer

Delivery speed matters substantially to Gen Z: 48% rated delivery within three days essential [[NORTHSTAR/GENZ-TRENDS@v2:P3.B4]]. Northstar's personalization offer is creating delivery friction, as personalized orders were 2.4 times more likely than standard orders to generate a "where is my order" ticket [[NORTHSTAR/SUPPORT-THEMES@v1:P2.B3]]. The pilot's roughly 12-day lead time was also the most common reason customers gave for not ordering again [[NORTHSTAR/FY27-MEMO@v1:S1.B3]].

### Key findings

- 48% of Gen Z respondents rated delivery within three days essential, with the share up sharply among those buying through social platforms [[NORTHSTAR/GENZ-TRENDS@v2:P3.B4]].
- Speed matters most for everyday routine items and least for gifts or special items, where shoppers expect a wait [[NORTHSTAR/GENZ-TRENDS@v2:P3.B4]].
- Missed delivery promises were a common source of cancelled orders [[NORTHSTAR/GENZ-TRENDS@v2:P3.B4]].
- Personalized orders were 2.4 times more likely than standard orders to generate a "where is my order" ticket [[NORTHSTAR/SUPPORT-THEMES@v1:P2.B3]].
- Made to order pairs took an average of 12 days to arrive, customers could not see production milestones in the tracker, and agents had few answers beyond the original estimate [[NORTHSTAR/SUPPORT-THEMES@v1:P2.B3]].
- Personalized buyers returned within 90 days at 18% against 24% for the matched control group, and lead time of about 12 days was the most common reason given for not reordering [[NORTHSTAR/FY27-MEMO@v1:S1.B3]].
- Operations notes that a twelve day wait cuts against Gen Z delivery expectations [[NORTHSTAR/Q3-REVIEW@v1:SL11.N1]].
- Pilot results state that the long wait for delivery was the main reason people gave for not coming back [[NORTHSTAR/PERSO-PILOT@v1:S1.B2]].

### Interpretation

Because delivery speed matters least for gifts and special items, personalization positioned as a gifting feature may tolerate longer waits than everyday purchases would [inference]. Visible production milestones or a clearer, shorter delivery promise could reduce ticket volume even if production time stays long [inference].

### Gaps & unknowns

The evidence does not give the survey sample size or method behind the three-day delivery figure, nor whether it applies equally to athletic footwear versus apparel. It does not show how the ticket-rate gap would change if production time or tracker visibility improved. A segment cut of delivery expectations by purchase type, and an operational test of faster or better-communicated made-to-order delivery, would close these gaps.

The pilot does not isolate lead time as the cause of the lower repeat rate; it shows that customers cite the wait most often, alongside the repeat gap [inference]. Review RV-00655 is not in the evidence, so its content and any link to the pilot are unknown. Retrieving that review directly from the review dataset would close this gap.
